concept.title: Branding and the legal position
concept.shortdesc: By default the output uses GOV.UK Design System components and layout without any government branding, because the crown and the GDS Transport typeface are legally restricted.

conbody.note: The GOV.UK crown, crest, and the GDS Transport typeface may only be used by official GOV.UK services. Publishing with them from any other organisation misrepresents your site as government-run.

section.title: Neutral mode (the default)
section.p: brandingneutral modeofficial modefontsNeutral builds ship no restricted assets at all, and the stylesheet is overlaid so that none is ever requested by a browser:

ul.li: system fonts stand in for GDS Transport
a plain masthead carries your service name instead of the crown
the footer carries no crest and no crown-copyright or Open Government Licence statement — instead it shows your publication's copyright and attribution, drawn from the bookmap's bookmeta (see below)

section.p: This makes neutral mode safe for standards bodies, local government partnerships, and any publisher who wants the Design System's clarity without its insignia.

section.title: The iStandUK theme
section.p: Setting govuk.branding=istanduk layers the iStandUK brand on top of neutral mode: the header becomes a white bar carrying the iStandUK logo above a brand-blue rule, and the footer band takes the brand blue (Pantone 072). The logo artwork ships as outlined vector paths, so no fonts are required or distributed, and every neutral-mode guarantee still holds.

image.alt: Home page with a white header carrying the iStandUK logo and publication title, a search field, and a dark blue rule beneath the header.

section.title: NHS branding
section.p: brandingNHSSetting govuk.branding=nhs applies the NHS Design System's colour palette, focus colour, and typography to the same GOV.UK Design System components, and gives the pages the white NHS header with the blue NHS logo and an NHS footer.
section.note: The NHS identity — the NHS letters and logo — is restricted to NHS organisations; non-NHS bodies need permission from NHS England or the Department of Health and Social Care. The build warns whenever this mode is used.
section.p: This is NHS-branded GOV.UK Design System output, not a rebuild on the NHS's own nhsuk-frontend. The components keep their GOV.UK structure recoloured to the NHS palette, so a warning or a table looks like its GOV.UK counterpart in NHS colours rather than the NHS Design System's own component — and NHS-specific components (care cards and the like) are not provided. Frutiger, the NHS brand font, is licensed to NHS organisations and is not bundled, so the text falls back to Arial unless you install it on the host.

image.alt: Home page with a white NHS header carrying the blue NHS logo and the publication title, a search field, and a blue rule beneath the header.

section.title: Official GOV.UK branding
section.p: brandingofficial modeSetting govuk.branding=official gives the pages the full GOV.UK identity: the black header with the crown and GOV.UK logotype, and a footer carrying the Open Government Licence statement and © Crown copyright.
section.note: The GOV.UK crown and the GDS Transport typeface are legally restricted to genuine GOV.UK services. Use this mode only for an official GOV.UK service; the build warns whenever it is used.
section.p: GDS Transport is licensed and is not bundled: install the font on the host and it is used, otherwise the text falls back to Arial. The plugin ships no crown crest image — the crown appears only in the header logo, and the footer states the licence and copyright in text.

image.alt: Home page with the black GOV.UK header carrying the crown and GOV.UK logotype and the publication title, and a search field.

section.title: Footer credits from the bookmap
section.p: Whatever the branding, the footer credits the publication itself, drawn from the bookmap's bookmeta:

ul.li: an attribution line naming the author or publisherinformation when it differs from the owner.

section.p: The same credit appears on every page — content, home, glossary and the rest — so it travels with each page a reader might land on or print. A map with no bookmeta simply shows its title instead. This applies to neutral, iStandUK and NHS branding; official mode shows the Open Government Licence and Crown copyright there instead, as GOV.UK services do.
